title: Additive linear Jordan parts: intertwiners, tensor sums and scalar extension
statement: Let $k$ be a perfect field [def-weil-field], meaning every algebraic extension is separable. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space and $A:V\to V$ a $k$-linear endomorphism. A linear endomorphism is geometrically semisimple if it is diagonalizable after extending scalars to an algebraic closure; it is nilpotent if some positive power is zero. There are unique commuting endomorphisms $A_s,A_n$ with $A=A_s+A_n$, $A_s$ geometrically semisimple and $A_n$ nilpotent. Both belong to $k[A]$, the subalgebra of $\operatorname{End}_k(V)$ consisting of polynomials in $A$. If $B:W\to W$ is another such endomorphism and $f:V\to W$ is $k$-linear with $fA=Bf$, then $fA_s=B_sf$ and $fA_n=B_nf$. On $V\otimes_k W$, put $C=A\otimes1+1\otimes B$; then $C_s=A_s\otimes1+1\otimes B_s$ and $C_n=A_n\otimes1+1\otimes B_n$. Here the tensor product is universal for bilinear maps, and $(A\otimes B)(v\otimes w)=Av\otimes Bw$. If $K/k$ is any extension with $K$ perfect, the parts of $1\otimes A$ on $K\otimes_k V$ are $1\otimes A_s$ and $1\otimes A_n$. The zero vector space is allowed.

source.place: Preliminaries to Proposition 17.74, printed p.376, additive version of Theorem 9.11 and Propositions 9.13--9.15, pp.168--169. Tensor-sum and scalar-extension formulations are the linear-algebra input to the agent-written solution of the exercise 17.74.

proof.text: We first record explicitly how equality is detected after scalar extension. Choose a finite basis $(e_i)_{i=1}^d$ of a $k$-space $U$, with coefficient maps $e_i^*:U\to k$. For any extension $L/k$, the maps $\lambda\otimes u\mapsto(\lambda e_i^*(u))_i$ and $(a_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i a_i\otimes e_i$ are inverse $L$-linear maps between $L\otimes_k U$ and $L^d$, as checked on pure tensors by bilinearity. Thus $(1\otimes e_i)$ is a basis, dimension is preserved, and extension of linear maps is injective: their matrices keep their entries under the injective inclusion $k\hookrightarrow L$. Addition, composition, identity and powers commute with extension, by evaluating on $\lambda\otimes u$. For a tensor of two finite-dimensional spaces, finitely many tensors of basis vectors span by expansion, so it too is finite dimensional. If any space in an assertion is zero, its endomorphism is the unique map, its identity equals zero, and nilpotence has exponent one; all subsequent formulas still apply.

source.place: Preliminary coordinate verification for the scalar extensions used in Section 9(b), pp.168-169; routine formulas written by the worker.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-polynomial-jordan-chevalley-decomposition] to $A$, obtaining $N=q(A)$ and $S=p(A)$ with $A=N+S$, $N$ nilpotent and $S$ complement-semisimple. Polynomial expressions in the same endomorphism commute: $A^iA^j=A^{i+j}=A^jA^i$ and expand the two finite polynomial sums. By [lem-sfb-geometric-semisimplicity-field-extension], $S$ is geometrically semisimple. Set $A_s=S$ and $A_n=N$; this proves existence and membership in $k[A]$. Conversely, suppose $A=S'+N'$ with $S'N'=N'S'$, $S'$ geometrically semisimple and $N'$ nilpotent. The same comparison makes $S'$ complement-semisimple. The uniqueness assertion of [lem-sfb-polynomial-jordan-chevalley-decomposition] therefore identifies it with $(S,N)$. This proves uniqueness for all commuting decompositions, without requiring their parts to be polynomial a priori.

source.place: Preliminaries to Proposition 17.74, p.376; Theorem 9.11, p.168, additive construction, with the two precise Mathlib/comparison inputs cited.

proof.text: Let $K/k$ be an extension with $K$ perfect. The extended pair $S_K=1\otimes A_s$, $N_K=1\otimes A_n$ sums to $1\otimes A$ and commutes by the pure-tensor formulas in step 1. If $A_n^r=0$, then $N_K^r=1\otimes A_n^r=0$. By [lem-sfb-geometric-semisimplicity-field-extension], $S_K$ is geometrically semisimple, hence complement-semisimple over the perfect field $K$. The extended space is finite dimensional by step 1. Apply uniqueness in [lem-sfb-polynomial-jordan-chevalley-decomposition] over $K$ to this pair and to the polynomial decomposition of $1\otimes A$. This gives precisely the two scalar-extension equalities. In particular they hold for an algebraic closure of $k$, which is perfect.

source.place: Theorem 9.11, pp.168-169, comparison under scalar extension; additive version of p.376. The verification of the candidate pair is explicit.

proof.text: Here is the action of the semisimple part on primary spaces over an algebraically closed field. Write $A=S+N$ for the pair already constructed, and fix $r\geq1$ with $N^r=0$. Choose an eigenbasis $(v_i)$ for $S$, with $Sv_i=a_i v_i$. Since $SN=NS$, $N$ preserves each $S$-eigenspace, so $(A-a_i)^r v_i=N^r v_i=0$. Thus each $v_i$ lies in $E_{a_i}(A)$ of [lem-sfb-generalized-eigenspace-direct-sum]. Grouping a basis expansion by the finitely many $a_i$ expresses every vector as a sum of vectors in these primary spaces. Uniqueness of primary expansions in that cited statement shows that every vector of $E_a(A)$ is a combination of the $v_i$ having $a_i=a$. Therefore $S$ acts as $a$ on $E_a(A)$, including primary spaces equal to zero.

source.place: Section 9(b), Theorem 9.11, p.168, additive primary-space construction; details explaining its agreement with step 2.

proof.text: For $fA=Bf$, extend everything to one algebraic closure $\bar k$ of $k$. Step 3 identifies the extended parts with the parts over $\bar k$. Induction on $n$ gives $(B-a)^n f=f(A-a)^n$, so $f$ sends $E_a(A)$ into $E_a(B)$ for every $a\in\bar k$. Step 4 says that the two semisimple parts act by the same scalar $a$ on these spaces; hence $fA_s=B_sf$ on each $E_a(A)$, and on the whole space by the spanning assertion of [lem-sfb-generalized-eigenspace-direct-sum]. Subtracting from $fA=Bf$ gives $fA_n=B_nf$. The injectivity from step 1 descends both equalities to $k$. No inverse of $f$, and no invertibility of $A$ or $B$, has been used.

source.place: Proposition 9.13, p.169, primary-space intertwiner argument, applied to additive rather than multiplicative parts.

proof.text: On $V\otimes_k W$ set $S=A_s\otimes1+1\otimes B_s$ and $N=A_n\otimes1+1\otimes B_n$. Evaluation on $v\otimes w$ gives $S+N=C$ and $SN=NS$: endomorphisms on different factors commute, and on the same factor the given Jordan parts commute. Write $X=A_n\otimes1$, $Y=1\otimes B_n$, with $A_n^r=B_n^t=0$ for $r,t\geq1$. Then $XY=YX$, $X^r=Y^t=0$. Distributively expand $(X+Y)^{r+t}$ into words. Reordering each word gives $X^iY^{r+t-i}$, which vanishes because either $i\geq r$ or $r+t-i\geq t$. Thus $N$ is nilpotent, with no division by factorials in any characteristic.

source.place: Additive analogue of Proposition 9.15, p.169: commuting tensor operators and nilpotence calculated explicitly.

proof.text: To check the remaining property of the candidate $S$, extend to $\bar k$. The coefficient formulas of step 1 identify $\bar k\otimes_k(V\otimes_k W)$ with $(\bar k\otimes_k V)\otimes_{\bar k}(\bar k\otimes_k W)$: send $\lambda\otimes(v\otimes w)$ to $(\lambda\otimes v)\otimes(1\otimes w)$ and send $(\lambda\otimes v)\otimes(\mu\otimes w)$ back to $\lambda\mu\otimes(v\otimes w)$. Bilinearity checks both inverses. The geometric comparison [lem-sfb-geometric-semisimplicity-field-extension] gives eigenbases $(v_i)$ and $(w_j)$ for the extended $A_s,B_s$, with eigenvalues $a_i,b_j$. By [lem-sc-tensor-product-free-basis], applied over $\bar k$ to these finite bases, the $v_i\otimes w_j$ form a basis. On this basis $S(v_i\otimes w_j)=(a_i+b_j)(v_i\otimes w_j)$, so $S$ is geometrically semisimple. The candidate pair from step 6 therefore is a commuting semisimple-nilpotent decomposition of $C$. Convert geometric to complement semisimplicity by [lem-sfb-geometric-semisimplicity-field-extension] and apply uniqueness in [lem-sfb-polynomial-jordan-chevalley-decomposition]. It yields $C_s=S$ and $C_n=N$, as required. Repeated eigenvalue sums do not affect diagonalizability.

source.place: Proposition 9.15, p.169, tensor eigenvector calculation, adapted to the additive tensor sum; the universal tensor reassociation and uniqueness application are written out.
